claim: One click opens a filled cart-loop practice with sample history.
Reset demo restores the shipped sample, and leaving the demo clears its keys.
The VS Code extension records a hypothesis, test output, fix, and clue in a debugging receipt.
The VS Code extension can delete all saved receipts after a specific confirmation.
The separate Chrome extension records the same four receipt fields in a browser popup.
The practice asks for a testable hypothesis before test output or a fix.
Website demo entries stay in the separate demo browser namespace.
VS Code receipts use local extension storage and are not sent over the network.
The website demo works offline after the first visit.
A completed receipt exports as Markdown.
The VS Code and Chrome extensions are free to download.
The Chrome extension requests browser storage only and has no tab or file access.
The Chrome extension has no tab, history, clipboard, or host permission and sends no receipt content over the network.
The VS Code extension does not read workspace files, open editors, or clipboard contents.
Neither extension generates code or answers.
The product has no analytics or third-party runtime scripts.
